entities.name: Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: The Rubáiyát of Omar Khayyám is a seminal work of Persian poetry, created circa 1100 by the renowned Persian mathematician, astronomer, and poet Omar Khayyám. Comprising omar khayyam’s robāʿiyyāt (“quatrains”), this collection of quatrains has been translated into Persian-English and continues to be celebrated for its profound insights into the human condition. The rubáiyát offers a unique window into the medieval Persian worldview, reflecting the cultural and intellectual currents of the time. Its themes of love, loss, and the transience of life continue to resonate with readers worldwide. The rubáiyát's significance extends beyond its literary merit, as it represents a pivotal moment in the evolution of Persian literature and its transmission to the West. The quatrains' blend of mysticism, philosophy, and humor has captivated readers for centuries, making the rubáiyát an enduring masterpiece of world literature. The rubáiyát's global impact can be seen in its influence on Western literature, particularly in the Romantic movement, and its continued relevance in contemporary literature and popular culture.
